title: Maple Street before 1907. Dr Curtis' house on right with covered porch
description: Maple Street was once Hartland’s Main Street, connecting with High Street at the crest of the hill. From there, it descended through Burtt’s land, known as Burtt’s Hill, and passed the present-day location of the Legion. After crossing the old wooden Becaguimic Bridge, a sharp left turn led up to the north end of High Street. The current Main Street did not receive its name until 1860. Maple Street extended to the river, where the town’s water supply originated from a spring on the riverbank. On the right, the third house was first owned by Dr Curtis and later by Dr Chestnut.
